Productivity of Transcripts and Genes

Source: R/productivity.R
productivity.Rd

The biotype split used by the workflow (protein coding versus retained intron, nonsense-mediated decay, ...) is a proxy. These functions make productivity a computed, graded property of every transcript and summarise it per gene:

  • transcript_productivity() classifies each assayed transcript as "productive" (complete ORF, no predicted NMD, same ORF as the canonical isoform), "altered_productive" (complete ORF, no NMD, but a different ORF than the canonical isoform: alternative start, in-frame change, frameshift or stop in novel sequence), "unproductive" (no ORF, premature stop codon by the 50-nt rule, no stop codon, an unproductive biotype such as nonsense_mediated_decay, retained_intron, protein_coding_CDS_not_defined, protein_coding_LoF, or a longest ORF without coding potential), "noncoding" (transcripts of genes without any coding isoform) or "uncertain" (incomplete CDS annotation without a premature stop, a credible ORF unrelated to the canonical one, FANTOM uncertain_coding). The reason column explains each call and source tells whether it came from the sequence ("sequence", when the annotation has transcript sequences, see extract_transcript_sequences() and transcript_orfs()), the annotation ("annotation") or external evidence ("evidence"). Evidence columns take precedence, in this order: a productivity_evidence column added with add_annotation_columns(), a validated NMD exon (add_nmd_exons()), a Ribo-seq ORF matching the transcript's ORF (add_riboseq_orfs()), an APPRIS principal isoform (add_appris()).

  • productive_fraction() is the share of a gene's expression carried by productive (and altered productive) isoforms, per sample or per group, with the difference between the last and the first group level. A gene whose expression is flat while its productive fraction drops is a post-transcriptional regulation call that gene-level differential expression misses. With inferential replicates (inf_reps, Salmon bootstraps or Gibbs samples) it reports the uncertainty of each fraction, and with a reference (gtex_reference()) the difference to the healthy-tissue baseline.

  • productivity_fractions() splits the gene's expression over all productivity classes and, for unproductive isoforms, over the mechanism (nmd, retained_intron, no_orf, non_stop, other).

  • test_productive_fraction() tests the change in productive fraction between two groups on counts, with a quasi-binomial model per gene (pooled proportions per group, Pearson over-dispersion, t test on the log odds ratio, BH adjustment). A gene with fewer than 5 reads in its smaller class (productive or not), pooled over both groups, carries too little information on usage: it gets a log_odds_ratio of 0 and no statistic or p-value, and does not count in the BH adjustment. A gene without reads in one group gets NA there too.

  • run_productivity_enrichment() ranks genes by the change in productive fraction between the last and the first group level (rank_by = "delta"), by that change over its standard deviation (rank_by = "delta_z") or by the statistic of test_productive_fraction() (rank_by = "statistic"), and runs gene set enrichment (fgsea) on gene symbols, which captures regulated unproductive splicing (AS-NMD) directly. It takes an IsoformicExperiment, a productive_fraction() table or a test_productive_fraction() table, and one or several gene set collections.

  • poison_exons() lists exons that occur only in unproductive isoforms of genes that also have productive isoforms and that do not overlap any exon of a productive isoform (cassette poison / NMD exons, as opposed to retained introns or alternative splice sites); plot_genomic_context() outlines them with highlight_poison_exons.

  • benchmark_productivity() measures the rules against the annotation biotypes: recall of nonsense_mediated_decay and retained_intron transcripts by the sequence/structure rules alone, and the share of protein_coding and canonical transcripts called productive.

  • productivity_palette() gives colours for the classes.

Usage

productivity_palette()

transcript_productivity(
  self,
  gene_name = NULL,
  nmd_rule = 50,
  use_biotype = TRUE,
  use_sequence = TRUE,
  use_evidence = TRUE,
  coding_cutoff = 0.364,
  ...
)

productive_fraction(
  self,
  group = NULL,
  levels = NULL,
  assay = "abundance",
  include_altered = TRUE,
  as_matrix = FALSE,
  gene_name = NULL,
  min_expr = 0,
  min_gene_count = 0,
  inf_reps = NULL,
  reference = NULL,
  ...
)

productivity_fractions(
  self,
  group = NULL,
  levels = NULL,
  assay = "abundance",
  min_expr = 0,
  gene_name = NULL,
  ...
)

test_productive_fraction(
  self,
  group,
  levels = NULL,
  assay = "counts",
  include_altered = TRUE,
  min_expr = 0,
  min_gene_count = 0,
  gene_name = NULL,
  ...
)

run_productivity_enrichment(
  self,
  genesets_list,
  group = NULL,
  levels = NULL,
  assay = "abundance",
  min_size = 15,
  max_size = 500,
  rank_by = c("delta", "delta_z", "statistic"),
  include_altered = TRUE,
  min_expr = 0,
  min_gene_count = 0,
  inf_reps = NULL,
  workers = getOption("isoformic.workers", 1L),
  ...
)

poison_exons(self, gene_name = NULL, ...)

benchmark_productivity(self, nmd_rule = 50, use_sequence = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

self

An IsoformicExperiment. run_productivity_enrichment() also takes the table of productive_fraction() for two or more groups, or of test_productive_fraction() for rank_by = "statistic", so that one table serves several gene set collections; the arguments that build the table (group, levels, assay, include_altered, min_expr, min_gene_count, inf_reps) are then ignored.

gene_name

Optional genes (names or IDs) to restrict the result to.

nmd_rule

Distance (nt) from the stop codon to the last junction above which NMD is predicted; default 50.

use_biotype

Logical, also use unproductive biotypes and FANTOM coding status (default TRUE).

use_sequence

Logical, use the sequence-derived ORFs of transcript_orfs() when the annotation has sequences (default TRUE).

use_evidence

Logical, apply the evidence columns (default TRUE).

coding_cutoff

Coding probability below which a longest ORF (one that could not be projected from the canonical start) is not believed (default 0.364).

...

Used only by run_productivity_enrichment(), which passes them to fgsea::fgseaMultilevel(); the other functions do not use them (reserved for methods). Each fgsea call runs with BiocParallel::SerialParam() unless nproc or BPPARAM is given; prefer workers (see Workers in run_enrichment()).

group

Name of a col_data column defining groups; NULL for per-sample values. run_productivity_enrichment() requires it for an IsoformicExperiment and ignores it for a productive_fraction() table.

levels

Levels of group to use, in this order; the change is last - first. Samples of other groups are ignored, as if the object had been subset to these samples, so every returned value comes from the samples kept. NULL takes all the levels of group. The tests (test_productive_fraction(), test_apa()) need exactly two levels.

assay

Transcript assay to use (default "abundance"; "counts" for the test).

include_altered

Logical, count altered_productive isoforms as productive in productive_fraction() (default TRUE).

as_matrix

Logical, return the genes x samples matrix of productive fractions instead of the summary table.

min_expr

Minimum assay value for an isoform to contribute (default 0): isoforms below it count as zero.

min_gene_count

Minimum mean count of a gene, the sum of its isoforms in the "counts" assay, in every group (over all the samples kept without group); genes below it are dropped. Needs a "counts" assay whatever assay is. The default 0 keeps every gene. See Details.

inf_reps

Optional list of transcript matrices (inferential replicates with the transcripts in rows and the samples of the assay in columns, as counts, as read_inferential_replicates() returns them); NULL uses x@metadata$inf_reps when present and FALSE skips the replicates, which leaves out the standard deviations and delta_z and is much faster. For an assay other than "counts" the draws are put on its scale with the "counts" assay (see Details); an object without a "counts" assay takes the draws to be on the scale of assay. run_productivity_enrichment() reads the replicates only for rank_by = "delta_z".

reference

Optional tibble from gtex_reference(), or a GTEx tissue name, giving the healthy-tissue productive fraction per gene.

genesets_list

Named list of gene symbol vectors (see read_gmt()), or a named list of such lists: each collection is then tested on its own and the result has a collection column (see run_enrichment()).

min_size, max_size

Gene set size limits passed to fgsea.

rank_by

Statistic that ranks the genes in run_productivity_enrichment(): "delta" (default), the change in productive fraction, "delta_z", that change divided by its standard deviation over the inferential replicates, which moves the genes with an uncertain change towards the middle of the ranking, or "statistic", the test of test_productive_fraction() on the "counts" assay between the first and the last level of levels, as a signed normal quantile of its p-value (see Details); assay and inf_reps are then not used. "delta_z" needs inferential replicates; a change that is the same in every replicate (delta_z is NA in the productive_fraction() table) is ranked with the largest absolute delta_z of the table (at least 1), with the sign of the change. It reflects the quantification uncertainty only, not the variation between samples or the number of reads; "statistic" reflects both (see Details).

workers

Number of worker processes that run the fgsea calls of run_productivity_enrichment() (one per gene set collection) in parallel: a whole number, or "auto" for the CPUs available to the session. Defaults to the isoformic.workers option, or 1 (serial). Needs the mirai package above 1; see Workers in run_enrichment(), also for the random seeds.

Value

  • transcript_productivity(): one row per transcript with transcript_id, transcript_name, transcript_type, gene_id, gene_name, productivity (a factor with the levels of productivity_palette()), reason, source, has_cds, cds_complete, orf_length, nmd_predicted, stop_to_last_junction, orf_fraction_of_canonical, is_canonical and, with sequences, the ORF columns behind the call (orf_source, nmd_class, frame_vs_canonical, coding_probability, n_uorf).

  • productive_fraction(): one row per coding gene with gene_id, gene_name, mean_gene_expr, productive_fraction (mean over the samples kept), with group one productive_fraction_<level> column per level and delta_productive_fraction, with inferential replicates productive_fraction_sd (the standard deviation over the draws, see Details) and, with group, delta_productive_fraction_sd and delta_z, and with reference the reference_* columns and delta_vs_reference. A genes x samples matrix with as_matrix = TRUE.

  • productivity_fractions(): one row per gene and class present (productivity, a factor), with fraction and, with group, the fraction_<level> and delta_fraction columns.

  • test_productive_fraction(): one row per coding gene with mean_gene_expr, the two productive_fraction_<level> columns, delta_productive_fraction, log_odds_ratio, se, statistic, dispersion, df, pvalue and padj, ordered by pvalue.

  • run_productivity_enrichment(): the fgsea result with the columns experiment ("productive_fraction"), rank_by and, for a list of collections, collection.

  • poison_exons(): one row per exon with gene_id, gene_name, seqid, start_pos, end_pos, strand, n_unproductive, transcript_ids and exon_length.

  • benchmark_productivity(): a list with the summary (metric, n, value, source) and confusion (transcript_type, productivity, n) tibbles.

  • productivity_palette(): a named character vector of colours.

Details

Low-count genes. A productive fraction computed from a few reads is mostly sampling noise: a gene with 4 reads moves by 0.25 when one read changes isoform. delta_z does not catch this, because the inferential replicates measure how the reads are split between isoforms, not how many reads were sampled. min_gene_count removes genes whose mean count (the sum of the counts of their isoforms in the "counts" assay) is below it in any group, before the statistics and the BH adjustment; with rank_by = "statistic", before the ranking. The filter is off by default (0); 10 reads is a reasonable start. The rule asks for enough reads in every group, because a fraction is compared between groups: it is stricter than the transcript filter of test_usage() (min_count reads in as many samples as the smallest group), and min_expr sets single isoform values to zero rather than removing genes. rank_by = "statistic" accounts for the reads of every gene and for the variation between its samples. Its dispersion is estimated for each gene alone, on n - 2 degrees of freedom and not moderated, so with three samples per group the ranking is still noisy. The t statistic is put on the normal scale through its p-value (sign(statistic) * qnorm(pvalue / 2, lower.tail = FALSE)), because the degrees of freedom differ between genes when samples without reads drop out. Its sign is that of the pooled change (delta_productive_fraction of test_productive_fraction()), which can differ from the mean of the per-sample fractions in productive_fraction() when the samples differ much in depth. Genes with fewer than 5 reads in one class get no statistic and are left out of the ranking, so that a change in the expression of the whole gene does not rank it.

Uncertainty of the fractions. With inferential replicates, productive_fraction() computes the productive fraction of every gene and sample in each draw. The draws are counts; for another assay each draw is first put on the scale of that assay, multiplied by assay / counts of the same transcript and sample (for TPM, the inverse of the effective length times the scaling of the sample), so that the fractions of the draws and of the assay, and min_expr, are on one scale. Where the point count or value is zero (Gibbs draws often give reads to such cells) the factor is estimated: from the length assay when the assay follows it (TPM of read_salmon() and read_oarfish()), otherwise from a transcript effect plus a sample effect on the log scale fitted on the other cells, and for a transcript without any count from its annotated length. productive_fraction_sd is the sample standard deviation of a gene's fraction over the draws, around the mean of the draws, averaged over the samples kept; delta_productive_fraction_sd is the standard deviation over the draws of the change between the group means, and delta_z is delta_productive_fraction divided by it. In every draw, only the samples in which the assay gives the gene a fraction are used. Both measure the spread of the draws, not their distance to the point estimate: the mean of Gibbs draws can differ from the EM estimate of the assay.

Examples

iso <- example_isoformic()
prod <- transcript_productivity(iso, gene_name = "RBPJ")
prod[, c("transcript_name", "transcript_type", "productivity", "reason", "source")]
